# Session-Establishment Requirements Quality Checklist: 038-acceptor-sendingtime-guard

**Purpose**: Validate the quality (completeness / clarity / consistency / measurability / coverage) of the 038 requirements — the acceptor first-Logon SendingTime guard (G1) + the reconnect callback-seam (G2) + the FIXT 1137 witness (G3) — before `/speckit-implement`. "Unit tests for English": each item tests whether the requirement is well-written, NOT whether code works.
**Created**: 2026-06-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit-checklist`; dispositioned by the mandatory `/speckit-checklist-audit` gate (pipeline step 9).

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the dispositions for all four bad-`52` input classes (absent/empty, malformed, stale-past, stale-future) explicitly specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/FR-003] — PASS: FR-002 covers stale-past/future; FR-003 covers absent/empty and malformed; data-model disposition matrix (§Group 1) rows them all with explicit outcome + reason code.
- [x] CHK002 Is the reject frame's exact field set (`35=3`, `371=52`, `372="A"`, `373=10`) AND the no-Logout decision documented as a requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, contract C-1] — PASS: FR-002 specifies `Reject 35=3, RefTagID(371)=52, SessionRejectReason(373)=10`, no-Logout explicitly stated ("not followed by a Logout"); contract C-1 §2 pins `RefMsgType(372)="A"` as well.
- [x] CHK003 Is the guard's position in the acceptor first-Logon validation order specified relative to `interpret_logon` / `ensure_hydrated_` / `reset_on_logon` / `check_inbound` / `1137` / `authorize_logon`? [Completeness, plan §Summary, data-model §guard-position] — PASS: data-model §Group 1 intro and guard-position note state the full order `interpret_logon → ensure_hydrated_ → SendingTime(52) [NEW] → reset_on_logon → check_inbound → 1137 → authorize_logon → establish`; plan §Summary and contract C-1 precondition confirm it with line references.
- [x] CHK004 Are the reject post-conditions specified for BOTH the in-memory AND the durable inbound counter (not just one)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, data-model INV-4] — PASS: FR-004 states "inbound sequence number MUST NOT be advanced or persisted"; INV-4 distinguishes in-memory (seeded-not-advanced) from durable (unchanged, no `persist_inbound_advance_`), and covers the `withhold_inbound` corner discriminant (persistent+no-withhold → seeded `D`; persistent+withhold/memory → `seqnum_min`).
- [x] CHK005 Is the outbound-counter behaviour on a reject (hydrated `N`, store-accept) specified for the persistent-store reconnect case? [Completeness, data-model INV-4] — PASS: INV-4 explicitly states "the Reject's `assign_outbound` runs against the hydrated outbound counter … Reject is stamped with the durable next-outbound `N` … `store(N,…)` passes `seq == next_seqnum`"; quickstart cell 14 is the named direct witness.
- [x] CHK006 Are the Group-2 callback-containment post-conditions (attempt proceeds, baseline updates, no spurious re-emit) fully enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, data-model INV-7/8/9] — PASS: FR-006 specifies attempt continues to "policy-defined outcome"; FR-007 specifies transparency on non-throwing path; INV-7 (containment), INV-8 (no spurious re-emit because baseline still runs), INV-9 (transparent) enumerate all three post-conditions; contract C-2 cross-confirms.
- [x] CHK007 Is the Group-3 observable set (on-wire `371=1137`, `toAdmin` observation, disconnect) specified for BOTH absent and non-conformant `1137`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: FR-008 enumerates "Reject frame carrying `RefTagID(371)=1137` on the wire, its observation through the admin/application observation path, and the subsequent disconnect"; data-model §Group 3 table covers both absent (`373=1`) and non-conformant (`373=5`) rows; contract C-3 repeats both cases.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is "stale" quantified with a specific tolerance (MaxLatency, default 120 s) and direction (absolute `|52−now|`, both past AND future)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-002 states "diverges from the effective clock by more than the configured maximum latency (in either direction)"; Edge Cases paragraph specifies "the guard tests absolute divergence, not direction"; Assumptions §Latency policy reuse states "default 120 seconds"; data-model §Group 1 table header cites `T = cfg_.sending_time_threshold ? : 120 s`.
- [x] CHK009 Is the boundary case (`|52−now| == MaxLatency`) disposition unambiguous (conforming, within window)? [Clarity, data-model INV-5] — PASS: INV-5 states "`|52−now| == T` is conforming (within window) — same boundary semantics as established-Q3's `check_sending_time` (`≤ max_latency`)"; Edge Cases paragraph says "treated as conforming (within window)"; `check_sending_time` implementation uses `delta > max_dur` (strict greater-than), confirming `==` is pass.
- [x] CHK010 Is "not advanced" disambiguated from "not persisted" (seed ≠ advance) so FR-004 is not read as a single conflated claim? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, data-model INV-4] — PASS: FR-004 says "MUST NOT be advanced or persisted"; INV-4 explicitly calls out "Seed ≠ advance — FR-004's 'MUST NOT be advanced or persisted' holds in-memory AND durable"; data-model §Group 1 defensive cells list "inbound counter seeded-not-advanced" as a separately-named arm; the quickstart cell-9 is a distinct named witness for persistent-path discrimination.
- [x] CHK011 Is the reason-code choice for absent/empty `52` (`reason=10`, NOT `RequiredTagMissing=1`) stated with its rationale (internal consistency with established-Q3)? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications] — PASS: Clarifications 2026-06-14 states the reason and rationale: "One uniform disposition for the same defect; matches `session.cpp` established-Q3 (which already maps empty `52` → reason=10). Diverges from QuickFIX-cpp/QFJ only on the absent-`52` reason code (they use `RequiredTagMissing`=1), an accepted, documented divergence in favour of internal consistency." FR-003 repeats the uniform reason=10 + absent/empty coverage. Research D-2 grounds it in code.
- [x] CHK012 Is the threshold expression (`cfg_.sending_time_threshold` optional → 120 s) unambiguous about whether 120 s is a config-field default or a code fallback when the optional is empty? [Ambiguity, contract C-1] — PASS: contract C-1 states explicitly "let `T = cfg_.sending_time_threshold ? duration_cast<seconds>(*…) : 120 s`" — clearly a code fallback when the `std::optional` is empty (not a config-field default); `session_config.hpp:185` confirms the field is `std::optional<std::chrono::milliseconds>` (no default set). No ambiguity.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Is the reject frame shape (no Logout) consistent across spec / data-model / contract / quickstart (no doc implying a Logout)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002] — PASS: spec FR-002 says "reject frame is not followed by a Logout"; data-model INV-2 says "emits the Reject then transitions straight to `Disconnected` with no Logout"; contract C-1 §2 says "No Logout is emitted"; quickstart cells 1–5 assert "NO Logout frame". No artifact implies a Logout on the first-Logon path; the established-Q3 Logout is explicitly distinguished as a "live-session teardown" in all four artifacts.
- [x] CHK014 Is the guard placement stated identically across all six artifacts (no residual "after the 1137" / "before `ensure_hydrated_`")? [Consistency, plan/research/data-model/contract/quickstart/tasks] — PASS: all six artifacts agree on placement `after ensure_hydrated_(:1925) BEFORE reset_on_logon(:1927)/check_inbound(:1936)` and therefore before `1137` and `authorize_logon`. Plan §Summary, research D-5, data-model §guard-position, contract C-1 precondition, quickstart §Group 1 intro, and tasks T006 all state this consistently. The old "after the 1137" placement was corrected in Gate-A round-1 rewrite; no residual in any artifact.
- [x] CHK015 Is the `reason=10`-for-all disposition consistent between FR-003, Clarifications, Edge Cases, and Assumptions (no divergent phrasing)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003] — PASS: FR-002 says "SendingTime-accuracy rejection (`Reject 35=3, RefTagID(371)=52, SessionRejectReason(373)=10`)"; FR-003 repeats "SAME disposition as FR-002 (`Reject`, `373=10`, `371=52`)"; Clarifications says "absent/empty, present-but-malformed, and stale all share a single `Reject(SessionRejectReason=10 SendingTimeAccuracy, RefTagID=52)`"; Edge Cases says "reason=10"; Assumptions §Missing `52` says "uniform `reason=10` reject". All consistent.
- [x] CHK016 Does the G2 framing (seam-hardening, production-unreachable, SC-free) align between spec US2/FR-006/FR-007 and the data-model/contract (no residual "production user guarantee")? [Consistency, Spec §US2] — PASS: US2 states "NOT a production user-facing guarantee against an operator-registered throwing callback (no such reachable surface exists today)"; FR-006 carries the parenthetical "(The live `Session`-path callback is engine-owned and `noexcept`, so this throw is unreachable in production today; FR-006 hardens the injection seam, not a reachable operator-callback guarantee.)"; data-model §Group 2 opens "In the live `Session`-path … the throw is unreachable in production"; contract C-2 repeats "this contract hardens the standalone-FSM injection seam, not a reachable operator-callback guarantee." SC-free is stated at spec §SC notes and data-model INV-* footnote. All consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality (Measurability)

- [x] CHK017 Are SC-001..003 each objectively verifiable by a test (no-establish; reject fields; byte-identical conforming) without implementation knowledge? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001..003] — PASS: SC-001 specifies "does not establish the session" + "emits the SendingTime-accuracy rejection (`373=10`, `371=52`, no Logout) + disconnect" driven off "controllable clock"; SC-002 specifies "explicitly rejects it (`reason=10`) and does not establish the session (no silent tolerance)"; SC-003 specifies "establishes the session with emitted output identical to the pre-change behaviour — verified by a no-regression (capture-and-compare) check". All three are verifiable by external observable assertion without inspecting internals.
- [x] CHK018 Is SC-004 stated as a measurable observable set (on-wire frame + observation + disconnect) rather than a vague "tested"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004] — PASS: SC-004 states "covered by session-level negative witnesses asserting the on-wire reject frame, its observation, and the disconnect — where none existed before." Three distinct, observable measurement points (wire frame, `toAdmin` observation, transport disconnect) are named explicitly.
- [x] CHK019 Is the conforming-path no-regression criterion expressed as "emitted output byte-identical" (measurable) rather than "behaves the same"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, data-model INV-6] — PASS: SC-003 explicitly says "emitted output identical to the pre-change behaviour"; FR-005 says "emitted output byte-for-byte identical"; INV-6 says "emitted output identical to pre-feature". The measurable predicate is byte-level identity, not a vague behavioural claim.
- [x] CHK020 Is the deliberate ABSENCE of a success criterion for Group 2 documented with rationale (intentional, not a gap)? [Measurability, Spec §SC notes] — PASS: spec §SC notes carries an explicit note "Group 2 (FR-006/FR-007) is intentionally carried by unit-test evidence only and has no success criterion: it is a marginal graceful-degradation hardening, not a measurable user-facing outcome, and inflating it into an SC would overstate its significance." Rationale is present; the absence is deliberate and documented.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are the simultaneous-bad scenarios (bad-52 + bad-1137 / + bad-credentials / + too-low-seqnum) specified with a defined precedence (the `52` reject wins)? [Coverage, data-model §simultaneous-bad] — PASS: data-model §Group 1 simultaneous-bad ordering table covers all three contest cases (bad-52+bad-1137 → 52 wins; bad-52+bad-credentials → 52 wins; bad-52+too-low-seqnum → 52 wins), with each outcome (emitted frame, no Logout, Disconnected) specified. The ordering rationale is grounded in the guard's placement before `check_inbound`/`1137`/`authorize_logon`. Tasks T004/quickstart cells 10–12 are the named witnesses.
- [x] CHK022 Is the persistent-store reconnect scenario (durable outbound `N>1`) covered as a distinct requirement, not folded into the generic case? [Coverage, data-model INV-4] — PASS: INV-4 has a dedicated paragraph for the persistent-store reconnect case ("on a persistent-store reconnect with durable outbound `N>1` the Reject is in-sequence"); quickstart cell 14 is a named, dedicated witness ("persistent-store reconnect, durable outbound `N>1`, bad-`52`"); contract C-1 §2 specifies "on a persistent-store reconnect the Reject is in-sequence on the wire and `store(N,…)` is accepted". The scenario is not folded into the generic case.
- [x] CHK023 Is the conforming (happy-path establish) scenario specified as a no-regression requirement, not only the failure path? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005] — PASS: FR-005 explicitly covers the conforming path as a requirement: "A conforming inbound first-Logon … MUST establish the session with emitted output byte-for-byte identical to today's acceptor establishment path." SC-003 is the corresponding AC. Quickstart cell 13 and tasks T004/cell-13 are the named witnesses.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK024 Is the future-dated `52` edge case (`52 > now + MaxLatency`) explicitly covered, not just stale-past? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: Edge Cases paragraph says "a `SendingTime(52)` that is ahead of the effective clock by more than the maximum latency must be rejected the same as a stale (past) one — the guard tests absolute divergence, not direction"; FR-002 says "in either direction"; quickstart cell 2 ("stale-future") and data-model matrix row for "stale-past OR future" both cover it.
- [x] CHK025 Is empty-`52=` distinguished from absent-`52` (different parse path) in the requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003, quickstart cell 5] — PASS: FR-003 says "absent/empty OR present-but-unparseable"; Edge Cases says "a Logon with no `52` header field (or an empty `52`)"; data-model §Group 1 defensive cells list "empty `52=` distinct from absent-52 — the empty-string short-circuits before `fix_string_to_utc_time`; witness it independently"; quickstart cell 5 is a named independent cell for empty-`52=`. The distinction is documented and separately witnessed.
- [x] CHK026 Is the latency-checking gating condition (`effective_clock_` presence; reuse of existing enable/disable semantics) addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: Edge Cases paragraph states "if and only if the existing configuration permits disabling inbound latency checking, the acceptor first-Logon guard honours that toggle identically to the established-session path (no new toggle is introduced)"; plan §Summary says "gate on `effective_clock_`"; data-model intro cites "with `effective_clock_` set"; contract C-1 §precondition says "`effective_clock_` is set". The gating condition is fully specified.
- [x] CHK027 Is the `withhold_inbound` corner (`141=Y` / `reset_on_logon` → `seqnum_min` even on a persistent store) documented so the inbound post-state is unambiguous? [Edge Case, data-model INV-4] — PASS: INV-4 has a dedicated `withhold_inbound` corner paragraph stating "when the acceptor header pre-scan shows `peer_sent_reset` (141=Y) OR `cfg_.reset_on_logon` … `ensure_hydrated_` WITHHOLDS the inbound seed, so the in-memory next-inbound stays at `seqnum_min` even on a persistent store; FR-004's 'not advanced' holds either way." Cell 9 discriminant is fully documented. (T017 confirmed DONE in tasks.md.)

[Completeness, Spec §FR-010/FR-011] — PASS: FR-010 states "MUST NOT introduce any new public wire field, new error code/slot, new configuration option … code generation change, or C-ABI change"; FR-011 states "MUST be confined to the session and reconnect surface" with explicit exclusion list. Tasks T021(iv) wires an observable test gate (`git diff … -- include/fix/c_api.h include/fixpp/session/session_config.hpp` shows NO additions + `check_layers.py` clean).
- [x] CHK029 Is the performance posture (admin-path-only, no per-message heap) specified so the Article VIII bench disposition is grounded? [Non-Functional, plan §Performance Goals] — PASS: plan §Performance Goals states "no change on the conforming path — the guard adds one parse + one `check_sending_time` comparison per inbound Logon (admin path, not the hot app path); the reject emits only on the non-conforming (terminal) path. No heap (stack `build_reject` buffer, mirroring the `1137` reject). `[const §XV.1]` preserved by construction." Tasks T021(v) carries the explicit Article VIII §3 self-waiver rationale ("admin-path-only, no perf surface").
- [x] CHK030 Is the fail-closed requirement for a `build_reject` failure (≥512 B buffer, never silent-success) specified? [Completeness, plan/contract, `[[feedback_fixed_buffer_build_failure_silent_success]]`] — PASS: contract C-1 §2 states "on `build_reject` failure FAIL CLOSED — `record_state_transition_(fsm_state::Disconnected)`, never silent-success (`[[feedback_fixed_buffer_build_failure_silent_success]]`)"; plan §Summary specifies "≥512B stack buffer; build-fail → FAIL CLOSED `Disconnected`"; quickstart cell 8 is the named defensive witness. Buffer size is pinned explicitly (both siblings use `std::array<std::byte,512>`).

[Assumption, Spec §Assumptions/Normative References] — PASS: spec §Assumptions "Reference-engine grounding" paragraph states both QFcpp (`Session::next` → `isGoodTime` → `doBadTime`, role-agnostic on the Logon) and QFJ (`isGoodTime`/`doBadTime`) validate inbound SendingTime on the Logon; explicitly distinguishes frame-shape divergence (fixpp: no Logout; QF: Reject + Logout) with rationale; Normative References cites `[FIX-SL §4.2.3]` → S-019. Research D-1 provides the source-code-level ground truth for both engines.
- [x] CHK032 Is the assumption that `interpret_logon` does NOT validate `52` (so the guard is the sole disposition site) recorded? - [x] CHK033 Is the deferred LIVE bad-SendingTime interop witness (L-021-3 / L-037-2 family) recorded as a known limitation rather than an unstated gap? ## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK034 Is the distinction between the 038 no-Logout shape and the established-Q3 Logout shape made explicit (pre-establishment vs live-session teardown) so the two are not read as a conflict? [Conflict, Spec §FR-002, data-model INV-2] — PASS: FR-002 explicitly states "not followed by a Logout — matching the in-arm pre-establishment `1137` reject sibling, NOT the established-session (Q3) path whose Logout is a live-session teardown"; data-model INV-2 says "matches the in-arm `1137` reject; the established-Q3 Logout is a live-session teardown, not applicable pre-establishment"; Clarifications 2026-06-14 paragraph explains the rationale ("pre-establishment first-Logon rejects do not Logout"). The distinction is unambiguous across all four artifacts.
